rules.description: Suppress a fresh high 1 that follows a completed high-1(s)-then-high-2 sequence without an intervening deeper pullback: the counter has just advanced to 1 again, and the PREVIOUS count cycle had already reached at least minPriorCount. Brooks: 'after a series of winning trades, be suspicious of renewed strength without first seeing a larger pullback - it might be a trap setting up.'
rules.pseudocode:
// one extra persistent value beside HighLowBarCount: prevCycleMaxCount, latched when the count resets
count == 1 && justAdvanced && prevCycleMaxCount >= minPriorCount

complexity.reason: one additional latched integer on top of the HighLowBarCount state

rules.merge_notes: Single source, mined as research grade because it appeared to need 'a memory of prior setup TYPES, a new kind of state'. Under R17-01's counter it does not: the sequence H1(,H1), H2, then H1 again IS the counter reaching >= 2, resetting on a fresh N-bar high, and re-advancing to 1, so one latched integer covers it. That is why it is B and not C. Used NEGATED it is the filter Brooks states ('it is wise to wait'), so the per-placement toggle gives both readings. The 'final flag' framing R11-24 references is a three_push_patterns concept and is not carried.

rules.description: A triggered high-N long (low-N short) fails: after HighLowBarCount reached countTarget, price trades back beyond the signal bar's opposite extreme. Brooks reads a failed high 4 / low 4 as the side losing control, and permits or takes the reversal trade in the other direction.
rules.pseudocode:
countReached = HighLowBarCount fired at countTarget on bar k;
close[0] < signalLow[k]   // long side failed -> permit/take the short

complexity.reason: the HighLowBarCount counter plus its already-retained signalLow and a bars-since cap

rules.merge_notes: Six statements of one event and its consequence. The event is identical in all six - a high-N or low-N setup triggered and then price went back through the signal bar - and the machinery is already inside HighLowBarCount (signalLow is retained there, so the failure test is free). countTarget default 4, the case Brooks names most (R00-62, V00-55, T00-48 all say low 4); T04-08 states it at 1 (fading a failed low 1 in a bottoming bear trend) and VP1-11 at 2/3 (a failed low 2 as a failed bear flag), so the same input covers all of them. Two sources add a conjunct that is NOT carried and is ANDed by the pane instead: T00-48 requires a bear trend-line break before the bears count as having regained control (a lines_channels_trendlines rule; TLValue recorded in el_words_needed for it), and VP1-11 requires the resulting breakout in the new direction (a breakouts rule). T00-48's framing is the negate toggle on this rule - block with-trend entries while the failure stands - so it needs no second rule. R00-62's 'wait for more price action' is advice with no test and is dropped from the reading.

rules.description: Block new longs for blockBars bars after a failed new high: price closed above the highest high of the last N bars and then, within failBars bars, a bear trend bar closed back below that level. Brooks: assume the market trades down for at least a couple of legs and at least 10 bars.

complexity.reason: a retained breakout level, a bounded failure window and a countdown; the swing-high reference is replaced by the N-bar-extreme window

rules.merge_notes: Single source. Mined as hard on a swing-high reference; the fresh-N-bar-extreme window used elsewhere in this bucket replaces the pivot and drops it to moderate. The 10-bar, two-legged correction horizon is the same number PostClimaxCorrectionBlock carries, from a different trigger - kept separate because the trigger is a failed breakout, not a climax, and breakouts_pullback_retest owns the failure detector (FailedBreakoutReversal) that this could eventually be keyed on. TP3-23's other two outcomes on page 311 (enough follow-through = stay long; sideways = buy lower) are not conditions and are dropped.

rules.description: The high 1 in a strong bull spike: after spikeBars consecutive bull trend bars, the first bar whose low is below the prior bar's low is the signal bar, and the entry fires when a bar within maxWaitBars closes above that signal bar's high. Mirror: the low 1 after a bear spike.

complexity.reason: a 'spike seen, first pullback seen' state pair carried across an unknown number of bars, plus one retained price

catalog_match.note: the trigger term is CloseAbovePriorHigh against a RETAINED signal-bar high rather than a fixed lag, which the catalog rule cannot express

rules.merge_notes: Kept as a composite because it is a named Brooks setup ('buying a high 1 pullback in a strong bull spike', stated in all three) AND because the trigger is against a bar at a VARIABLE lag - the pane cannot AND CloseAbovePriorHigh(fixed lag) with a spike filter and get this. It is NOT HighLowBarCount at countTarget 1: this rule's reset is a completed spike, not a fresh N-bar high, and its trigger is a later bar closing over a retained level rather than the signal bar itself. spikeBars: T07-45 says 3, TP3-16 says 4, T23-04 says 3 - default 3. T23-04 is the same mechanism anchored at the session open ('trend from the open'), so its placement is INTRADAY-ONLY while the rule itself is not; the always-in / trend-from-open flag it also reads is a context_regime rule the pane ANDs. Brooks's caveat in TP3-16 and T07-45, 'but not after a buy climax', is PostClimaxCorrectionBlock and is ANDed, not carried here.

rules.description: The first pullback bar after a breakout does not arrive until at least minBarsBeforePullback bars have passed since the breakout bar: the current bar is the first bar since the breakout whose low is below the prior bar's low, and it is at least N bars after it. Brooks's leading sign of breakout strength; NEGATED it is his sign of weakness ('the first pullback occurs two bars after the reversal').
rules.pseudocode:
b = barsSince(close[0] > highest(high, breakoutLookback)[1]);
b >= minBarsBeforePullback && low[0] < low[1] && lowest(low, b)[1] >= low[1]   // no earlier pullback bar since the breakout

complexity.reason: a bars-since-breakout counter plus a 'no earlier pullback bar' window test

rules.merge_notes: Eight statements of one test, five of them the same sentence copied across books ('The first pullback occurs only after three or more bars of breaking out' - R00-58, R02-14, V00-48, T00-33). Three add something. R05-02 is the same rule at minBarsBeforePullback = 0/1: it is the bare marker 'the first bar since the breakout with a low below the prior bar's low', which is where the 'no earlier pullback bar' clause in the pseudocode comes from and is the most mechanizable phrasing of the first-pullback anchor. R02-23 is the rule NEGATED (a pullback within 2 bars = weakness) - the per-placement toggle, both thresholds recorded. T15-40 is the OTHER bound, 'any pullback should come within five bars or so' - negated at minBarsBeforePullback = 6; its raceBars conjunct (consecutive higher highs since the breakout) is bar_anatomy_trend_doji's ConsecutiveTrendBars and is ANDed by the pane, not carried. V02-13 is the one source that mechanizes the anchor fully - 'the first down-close since a bull reversal bar k bars ago with k-1 up closes between' - and is the reason the grade is moderate rather than research; its anchor is a reversal bar rather than a breakout, which is a placement choice, not a different rule. Default 3, unanimous among the sources that state it. The breakout anchor uses the same fresh-N-bar-extreme test as HighLowBarCount so the two share one window.

rules.description: Brooks's bar counting, the H1/H2/H3/H4 and L1/L2/L3/L4 family. A persistent count of completed pullback legs since the trend last made a fresh resetLookback-bar high. A bar whose high exceeds the prior bar's high advances the count, but only once a new low has formed since the last counted bar (otherwise it is a retest of the same leg, not a new one); the count resets to 0 the instant the close makes a fresh resetLookback-bar high. Fires on the bar that advances the count to countTarget - that bar is the high-N signal bar, and under the corpus's stop-entry convention (signal-bar close, next-bar open) the fire IS the entry. Mirror: low 1..low 4.

complexity.reason: a cross-bar counter plus two remembered prices and one Highest window; no pivot detection and no lookahead

catalog_match.note: nothing in the catalog holds cross-bar counter state of this kind

rules.merge_notes: Twenty-three statements of one primitive, the single most load-bearing rule in the trilogy. THE DEFINITION THAT WINS IS R17-01 (Ranges ch17), for the reason MERGE.md gives: it needs no swing pivots, no lookahead and no leg definition - a bar advances the count on a higher high only after a new low since the last counted bar, and the count resets on a fresh N-bar high. Every other definition here is a citation, not a rule. The losing definitions, in the order they cost more machinery: (a) swing-pivot leg segmentation - R05-17, V24-03, TP1-05, T18-02, T20-02, V01-05, all graded hard and all needing SwingHigh/SwingLow plus pivot retention; (b) 'count each higher-high bar since the pullback began, resetting when the trend makes a new extreme' with the extreme left undefined - R00-61's R00-60, T00-20's T00-19, TP1-06 (this is R17-01 minus the concrete reset, which is exactly what R17-01 sharpens); (c) the ad hoc per-chapter counters T10-23 (reset on a new trend high, resetLookback 20 - the closest independent restatement of R17-01, and strong corroboration), T15-19 (resetOnNewHighBars 10), T21-72 (maxPullbackBars 20). The 'at least one bar that did not make a higher high between counts' phrasing (T10-23, T15-19, T21-72) is behaviourally the same guard as R17-01's 'a new low since the last counted bar' in a real pullback, but R17-01's is the cheaper and less ambiguous test and is the one carried. countTarget covers high 1 (R05-18, V00-52, R17-03, R01-09's 'first pullback', V01-10's pullback ordinal), high 2 (the most-stated setup: R05-19, V00-53, R17-04, T10-23, T15-19, T18-02, T20-02, T21-72, V01-05, TP1-06, T00-20, R00-61), high 3 (wedge bull flag) and high 4 (R17-06); Brooks caps the count at 4 and the counter saturates there. resetLookback defaults differ (R17-01/T10-23 20, T15-19 10, T21-72 20); 20 is carried. ABC corrections are this counter under another name - leg A is the run to count 1, leg B the failed bounce, leg C the run to count 2 - so no separate rule (R00-61, R17-01 and T01-05 all say so). ROLL-UP: swing_structure merged R17-01 alone under this same key with the same shape; the two entries are the same rule and only one should be authored. countTarget was added there for the same reason it is added here - a rule must fire on something. Folded the swing_structure copy (R17-01), the same persistent counter from the same source.

rules.description: The current pullback has completed AT LEAST minLegs legs - HighLowBarCount's counter read as a threshold rather than an equality. Brooks's 'a pullback, like all trends, will commonly have at least two legs': a with-trend entry is favoured only once the count has reached two.
rules.pseudocode: count >= minLegs   // the counter of HighLowBarCount, same state and same reset

complexity.reason: the HighLowBarCount counter with a >= comparison

rules.merge_notes: Kept apart from HighLowBarCount deliberately: == countTarget fires on ONE bar (the signal bar) while >= minLegs stays true for the rest of the pullback, so as a context filter ANDed into a pane they select different bars. All three sources state it as a context/quality read, not an entry: RP3-03 'a pullback commonly has at least two legs, fade the first leg's breakout and wait for the second'; V01-03 'it was two-legged, so the bears showed some strength' (its swing-pivot countLegs is the losing definition, replaced by the R17-01 counter); T19-21 'repeated two-legged pullbacks are setting up with-trend entries' - the REPETITION across successive pullbacks is dropped as having no bar-level test, so T19-21 is carried lossily as the single-pullback reading. Default 2 from all three.

rules.description: Block with-trend entries for blockBars bars after consecutive buy climaxes: no run of climaxCount consecutive climactic bull moves has completed within the last blockBars bars. Brooks: 'after three consecutive sell climaxes the market usually corrects sideways to up for at least 10 bars and with at least two legs.'

complexity.reason: a bars-since counter keyed on an existing climax detector

rules.merge_notes: Four statements of one block, unanimous on 10 bars and on 'at least two legs' as the expected correction. All four were mined at hard or research grade because 'climax' had no definition; bar_anatomy_trend_doji has since merged ConsecutiveClimaxBars as an authorable rule, so the only thing left here is the bars-since counter - hence B, not C. climaxCount 3 from RP1-14 and R22-15 (T21-40 and T21-71 say 'consecutive climaxes' and 'a buy climax' without a count, so 3 is the stated value and 1 is the loose reading). T21-71 adds the useful specific: after a climax a high 1 and maybe a high 2 will fail, so the block should lift at count >= 2 - that is HighLowBarCount ANDed, not a second rule. R22-15's session scoping ('the third consecutive sell climax of the day') is a time_session concern and is dropped; the bar window does the same work without a session reset. Carried as a filter, so a placement that wants the opposite reading (fade after three climaxes) uses the negate toggle.

rules.description: The pullback in progress has lasted no more than maxPullbackBars bars, measured as the bars since the trend last made a fresh resetLookback-bar high (the same anchor HighLowBarCount resets on). A brief pullback is Brooks's sign of strength; NEGATED, the rule is his sign of weakness ('the pullback extends for several bars').

complexity.reason: a bars-since counter keyed on the same fresh-extreme test HighLowBarCount already computes

rules.merge_notes: One rule and the per-placement negate toggle. R02-15 / T00-34 / V00-49 are the strength form (<= 2 bars); R02-24 is the same test negated at a different threshold (>= 4 bars, weakness). Both book values recorded, default 2 (three sources against one). R02-15's and V00-49's second conjunct - 'and it follows a bar that is not a strong bear reversal bar' - is NOT carried here: bar_anatomy_reversal_signal already merged it as PullbackNotAfterStrongOppositeReversalBar, and the pane ANDs it. The anchor is the design decision that lets this leave research grade: the sources say 'the pullback' without saying when it started, and the fresh-N-bar-high reset from R17-01 supplies a concrete start with no pivot search. R11-11 (dropped) states the same measure as a WINDOW, 5 to 10 bars, for a high 2 - if the authoring pass wants a band, minPullbackBars is the second input to add.

rules.description: The second leg of the correction has run beyond the first leg's extreme: the running low since the count reached 2 is below the low retained when the count reached 1 (mirror: the running high above the count-1 high). Brooks: 'bears who shorted the first up leg will add as soon as the second leg up goes above the high of the first leg up.'
rules.pseudocode: count >= 2 && minLowSince < signalLowAtCountOne   // both values already retained by HighLowBarCount

complexity.reason: one extra retained price on top of the HighLowBarCount state; the comparison itself is trivial

rules.merge_notes: Single source. Mined as hard because it was framed in terms of leg 1 and leg 2 identified by pivots; under R17-01's counter the two legs' extremes are the values the counter already keeps (signalLow at each advance, and the running minimum since), so no pivots are needed. This is the EXPANDING correction - distinct from LegCountAtLeast, which only asks how many legs there have been, and from HighLowBarCount, whose advance guard asks for a new low since the last COUNTED bar rather than beyond the FIRST leg's extreme. Those two coincide for a strictly deepening pullback and diverge for a shallow second leg, which is exactly the case Brooks is separating.

rules.description: The second entry: an earlier same-side signal triggered within the last withinBars bars, that first entry failed (price traded back beyond the first signal bar's opposite extreme), and a new same-side signal is triggering now. Brooks's most-repeated reliability filter, and the one condition he says is sufficient on its own.
rules.pseudocode: exists k in 2..withinBars: close[k] > high[k+1] && lowest(low, k-1)[0] < low[k+1] && close[0] > high[1]

complexity.reason: a bounded backward scan with two conditions per candidate bar; no pattern registry and no per-placement state

catalog_match.note: LastTradeCooldown gates on a REALIZED trade's outcome via PositionProfit/BarsSinceExit; this gates on a repeated raw pattern whether or not a trade was taken, and can fire before any trade exists

rules.merge_notes: Eight statements, and the fork that matters is what 'the same logic as the first signal' means. TWO OPTIONS were on the table. (1) A generic setup-identity registry - 'the same Entry candidate fired and failed' - which is what R00-52, V00-65, T00-21, T06-31 and R26-06 describe, all graded research, and which needs engine support the corpus does not have (a per-placement fire/fail log). (2) T21-28's CONCRETE PROXY: define the signal as the generic price trigger (a close above the prior bar's high) and the failure as price trading back below that signal bar's low, then scan the last withinBars bars for one. T21-28 WINS - it is a bounded scan over prices, needs no registry, and reproduces the second entry Brooks actually points at in the figures. It is lossy in exactly one way, and the loss should be recorded: it counts a second GENERIC trigger, not a second instance of whichever pattern is placed alongside it. Option 1 stays available if per-placement signal memory is ever added; bar_anatomy_reversal_signal reached the same conclusion for SecondReversalSignal and its 'track only the engine's own last Entry signal' decision is the third option. withinBars: T21-28 10, V24-18 8, V00-65 5, T06-31 10, R00-52 6, R26-06 10 - default 10. V04-13 is this filter with a climax anchor ('buy a higher low after a sell climax, not the initial reversal'), carried as a citation; the climax term is ANDed. Near-miss kept separate: SecondSignalNotBetterPrice is the price-quality gate ON this rule, not a restatement of it.

rules.description: Exit (and optionally reverse) the open position the moment the OPPOSITE side's bar count reaches countTarget. Brooks: 'if you ever buy early, always get out and even reverse if the market triggers a low 2 or 3 short'; mirrored for a short caught by a high 2 or 3.

complexity.reason: the same counter as HighLowBarCount read on the opposite side, plus a position test

catalog_match.note: the catalog rule is an Entry-side reversal permission keyed on dollars; this is an Exit keyed on the opposing count triggering

rules.merge_notes: ROLL-UP: swing_structure merged V21-04 ('countertrend traders trying to buy in a bear trend should always exit on a low 2 signal') under this same key with the same shape - one rule, two sources across two buckets, author once. Kept as its own rule rather than a placement of HighLowBarCount because it reads the OPPOSITE side's counter, which a mirrored Entry placement cannot supply, and because it is an Exit. R17-13's 'especially if there is a strong bear signal bar' is a bar_anatomy_reversal_signal term with no threshold given and is dropped; the 'optionally reverse' half is the engine's own reversal behaviour, not a condition. Folded the swing_structure copy (V21-04): the same exit on the opposing count reaching countTarget.
